source_evidence: In a Roth 401(k) account, employee contributions are not tax-deferred but are made with after-tax dollars.
question: Misconception: Roth 401(k) contributions are tax-deferred in the same way as traditional 401(k) contributions. Is that correct?
answer: No. Roth 401(k) contributions are made with after-tax dollars, while traditional 401(k) contributions are tax-deferred until the savings are withdrawn. Roth account earnings and withdrawals are generally tax-free.
